name: Connections Academy
line: Connections Academy is a full-time online public school. AMP is only math, for home or beside any school.
description: AMP vs Connections Academy: a tuition-free online public school, and a math program that finds each learner's level and chooses every problem.
verdict: Connections Academy is a full-time online public school from Pearson, free to families, with certified teachers, live classes and accredited courses [1][2][3][7][8]. It is a school, and math is one subject in it. AMP is only math: it finds the level in each strand, chooses every problem, explains every miss and brings skills back on a schedule, for a family that teaches at home or wants more math beside any school.

reasons.title: AMP adds math without changing schools
reasons.body: Connections Academy is a full-time public school: a child enrolls in the state's school, studies about 30 hours a week and takes the state's tests [3][5]. We found no way to buy its math on its own [1][2]. AMP is only math. A family that teaches at home can use it as the math course, and a child at any school can use it beside school, starting the same day.

reasons.title: The adult does not have to teach the math
reasons.body: Connections Academy asks a Learning Coach, a parent or trusted adult, to oversee schoolwork about 5 to 6 hours a day in elementary school and 2 to 3 hours in middle and high school [4]. The coach structures the day, gives one-on-one help and checks understanding [4]. In AMP the adult has nothing to plan, teach or grade. AMP places the learner, chooses each problem, checks it and schedules review.

reasons.title: Each part of math gets its own level
reasons.body: Connections Academy places students in courses using their academic records [3]. Its pages say each school's courses meet state standards, and advanced younger students may work at a higher grade level when appropriate [3][6]. We found no placement test or adaptive practice described on the pages we read [3][5][9]. AMP places the learner within the first 24 problems, keeps a separate level in each of 14 strands and chooses every next problem from the learner's answers, so a learner ahead in geometry and behind in fractions gets work at both levels.

reasons.title: Every miss comes with the worked answer
reasons.body: Connections Academy teaches with text, video, audio and interactive lessons, and its certified teachers evaluate student work [3][7][9]. We could not see how its math answers a wrong response: its sample lessons cover science, social studies, language arts and biology, but no math [10]. AMP shows right or wrong, the correct answer and worked steps after every problem, with a one-step hint and a written lesson there before the learner answers.

reasons.title: A published mastery rule and review schedule
reasons.body: Connections Academy's teachers evaluate student work and use assessment results to adjust support, alongside benchmark assessments and state tests [3]. We found no mastery rule, automatic return to earlier skills or scheduled review of math on the pages we read [3][9]. In AMP a skill is strong when four of the last five answers are right without help, and two misses in a row send practice back to what it builds on. Each learned skill comes back after 6 hours, 1 day, 3 days, 1 week, 2 weeks and a month, mixed with other topics.

reasons.title: Paper made for the learner, not the course
reasons.body: Elementary students at Connections Academy spend about 70% of their school day offline, and the school provides physical textbooks and workbooks [2][5]. AMP prints unlimited workbooks built from the learner's own answers, each with a worked answer key. Results entered from paper count toward the learner's level.

rows.price: Tuition-free, paid with state tax dollars. Families pay for supplies, optional field trips and internet [2][3].
rows.buyers: Families only, by enrolling a child full time in a state's Connections Academy school. Availability depends on the state; most schools have enrollment deadlines [2][3].
rows.range: Full elementary, middle and high school courses, kindergarten through grade 12, with honors, AP and dual enrollment at most schools [6].
rows.start: Students are placed in courses from their academic records [3]. No placement test or diagnostic described on the pages we read [3][5][9].
rows.teaching: Certified teachers, live online LiveLesson classes, and lessons with text, video and audio, plus physical textbooks [2][3][7].
rows.next: The course's daily lessons and assignments, shown in a planner [5]. No adaptive practice described on the pages we read [3][9].
rows.mastery: Teachers evaluate student work; benchmark assessments and state tests [3]. No mastery rule found on the pages we read.
rows.review: No scheduled review of earlier skills found on the pages we read [3][9].
rows.print: Physical textbooks and workbooks provided by the school. Elementary work is about 70% offline [2][5].
rows.adult: A Learning Coach oversees schoolwork for every subject: about 5 to 6 hours a day in elementary, 2 to 3 later [4].
rows.reports: A gradebook of grades and assessments, and a planner of daily lessons [5]. Grades and diplomas from an accredited school [3][8].
rows.evidence: No entry in Evidence for ESSA or the What Works Clearinghouse [12][13]. No outcome study found on the pages we read [6][8].

theirs: Connections Academy is a tuition-free online public school program run by Connections Education, part of Pearson [1][8]. Its schools are run state by state, for kindergarten through grade 12 [1]. Families enroll a child full time, and the state pays with tax dollars [2]. Pearson reports more than 100,000 students [1].

Students learn about 30 hours a week. Elementary students spend about 30% of the school day on a computer and 70% offline; middle school is about 75% online and high school 90% [5]. The day mixes live LiveLesson classes, where teachers reinforce hard concepts and students join by microphone and chat, with independent lessons and assignments [3][7]. A parent or other trusted adult serves as Learning Coach, and certified teachers teach and evaluate the work [3][4].

Math is one subject in a full curriculum that the school says comes from leading educational publishers and meets state standards. Course choices vary by school [3]. The pages we read do not name the math courses or their publisher. Pearson also runs Pearson Online Academy, a separate tuition-based private online school [19]. This page does not compare it.
credit: Free to the family. The state pays; families cover supplies, optional field trips and internet [2]. AMP costs $599 a year or $59 a month for the first child.
Certified teachers and live online classes [3][7]. AMP has no live teachers or tutors.
A whole school: full courses from kindergarten through grade 12, with honors, AP and dual enrollment at most schools [6]. AMP is only math and ends at precalculus.
Grades and a diploma. Connections Education is accredited by Cognia, and its NCAA-approved courses are listed [3][8]. AMP gives no course credit or transcripts.
Special education and IEP support, and a stated commitment to WCAG 2.2 Level AA accessibility with published conformance reports [1][11]. AMP has no read-aloud and no published conformance report.

theirs: On the pages we read, including its curriculum and accreditation pages, Connections Academy publishes no study of how much its students learn, in math or any subject [6][8]. Connections Academy has no entry in Evidence for ESSA or the What Works Clearinghouse (checked November 2026) [12][13].

Its headline numbers measure satisfaction. The home page says 97% of parents say their child is receiving a quality education, based on its 2026 parent survey [1]. The reviews page names the survey but gives no sample size or method [18].

The independent research on online schools covers the sector, not Connections Academy by name. Stanford's CREDO studied Pennsylvania charter students over four school years ending in 2016-17. It found "remarkably weaker growth in both reading and math" for online charter students, 25% of the state's charter students, than for the average non-charter or brick-and-mortar charter student [14]. The summary names no Connections Academy school.

The National Education Policy Center's 2021 review of virtual schools finds "little research evidence to support or justify the expansion" of virtual schools [15]. Its summary does not name Connections Academy or Pearson.
ours: AMP's rules for math come from findings that have held up. In a randomized trial of 787 seventh graders that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations, mixed, spaced practice scored 62% on a test about a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks. The test was the researchers' own [16]. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, in a mix of ages and subjects, feedback that explains averaged an effect of 0.49, the correct answer alone 0.32, and right-or-wrong only 0.05 [17]. We found no review schedule or mastery rule for Connections Academy's math on the pages we read. We expect a learner who meets these rules at every problem to learn more math, at home or beside a full-time school. That is our bet, and we have committed to testing it in public.

AMP is new, and its own outcome studies have not run yet. They begin in 2027: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each is registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. Until then, the research behind each part of AMP is laid out in our report, and the code is public.

them: You want a full-time public school at no cost, with certified teachers and live classes.
Your child needs grades and a diploma from an accredited school.
Your child needs special education or IEP services from a school.
Your child needs AP courses or dual enrollment.
amp: You teach at home and want math that places, checks and schedules review without you planning it.
Your child stays in their school and needs more math at the right level.
Your child is ahead in one part of math and behind in another.
You want every miss explained with worked steps, on screen and in the workbook answer key.
You want to start this week, without waiting for an enrollment window.

questions.question: Is Connections Academy free?
questions.answer: Tuition is free: the school is paid for with state tax dollars. Families pay for supplies, optional field trips and internet [2]. AMP costs $599 a year or $59 a month for the first child, and the first 100 answers are free.

questions.question: Is AMP a replacement for an online school?
questions.answer: No. AMP is math only, with no live teachers, other subjects, transcripts or diplomas. A family that homeschools on its own can use AMP as its math, and any student can use it beside school.

questions.question: My child is enrolled in Connections Academy. Can we use AMP too?
questions.answer: Yes. AMP is a separate program a family buys directly, and it runs in any current browser. It places the learner within the first 24 problems and keeps a level for each part of math. It does not replace the school's math course or its grades.

questions.question: How do online schools do in math?
questions.answer: Stanford's CREDO found much weaker growth in reading and math for Pennsylvania's online charter students than for non-charter or brick-and-mortar charter students, over four years ending in 2016-17 [14]. That study names no Connections Academy school, and we found no outcome study of Connections Academy itself on the pages we read [6][8].
